# Architecture and lane contracts

The monorepo has @crew/shared, @crew/server, @crew/web and @crew/cli. All packages are ES modules. Node SQLite is synchronous. Never await inside transaction(fn). Migrations export up(db) and run in filename order once. Ranges: 001 L0; 100–199 people; 200–249 W1; 250–299 W2; 300–349 I1; 350–399 I2.

Server lane modules export registerRoutes(ctx) from modules/<lane>/routes.js. ctx contains app, db (raw DatabaseSync), bus, config, requireAuth, asyncRoute, paginate, pagination, transaction(fn), id(), now(). People registers first and assigns ctx.permissions and ctx.authenticateToken(token). Authentication runs per request and sees those hooks. req.user is {id,email,name,createdAt,updatedAt}; req.auth is {kind:'session',sessionId,user} or people-defined token identity with kind:'token', scopes. All protected handlers use requireAuth then the people authorization service. Document that service's stable methods in people API docs before work begins.

Domain mutations call bus.emit({actorId,orgId,projectId,entityType,entityId,action,before,after,time}). bus adds UUID and default UTC time. Consumers are synchronous and return promptly; all event state persists through SQLite, with no second outbox or auth system. Storage column names use snake_case; public API uses camelCase. Insight subscribes after work registration, before requests begin. Register shutdown callbacks in ctx.cleanups; mark ctx.sseRegistered=true when replacing SSE.

Web lane pages/<lane>/routes.jsx exports routes [{path,component}] and navigation [{path,label}]. Hash route params are decoded; page props are params,query,user,api,store,navigate. Components include Page,Field,Button,Notice,Empty,Loading,DataTable,useLoad in components/ui.jsx. API helper get/post/patch/put/delete sends CSRF header and reports stable errors. Add focused CSS under styles and import from lane routes if required.

CLI commands/<lane>.js exports commands, an object keyed by group name. Each async command receives {command,args,options,client,configFile,print}. args are positional arguments after group; options maps --name values and --json booleans. client offers get/post/patch/delete/request. Return output via print(value). Reuse client query helper and output formatting. CLI dispatch automatically loads implemented lanes.

Tests live outside src/bin. Server test/helpers.js exports testServer() with ctx,url,agent(),close(). agent() returns request(method,route,body,headers) with cookie persistence, returning {status,data,response,cookie}. All paths omit /api/v1 when using the helper. Always close in finally. CLI tests use async child processes so the HTTP event loop remains live.

Each lane owns its feature checks in scripts/checks/<lane>.mjs with export async smoke(ctx) and restart(ctx). Acceptance ctx contains {request,clients,ids,dataDir,url,check,cli}; checks must use public HTTP and actual CLI, save ids to ctx.ids without credentials in reports. The lead integrates these actual checks into acceptance modes. Public API docs are lane-specific docs/api-people.md, api-work.md, api-insight.md.

People's implemented service and shared outbox schema are specified in [People API](api-people.md). Use assertion methods on every protected route, and filter list queries with projectIds before pagination for guests. Public health/signup/login routes do not require an account; all current protected auth/people/SSE handlers check the shared service. The integrated runtime audit enumerates current registered API routes and proves anonymous denial outside explicit public entrypoints. Dedicated actual HTTP, CLI and browser tests separately qualify role, token scope, project, team, recipient, current membership and revocation boundaries across all three lanes, including saved filters, transfer and live SSE. Credential-bearing account outbox links are browser-session only. A registration/anonymous-denial census does not establish every positive authority/input combination; see the People API's precise current audit boundary.

People migrations 101 and 102 extend the existing auth spine with invitations/password reset hashes, personal API token hashes and sanitized security_audit. Purpose-bound HMAC credential verification requires canonical unpadded base64url for both 32-byte nonce and signature, rejecting discarded-bit aliases before hashed database lookup. It uses CREW_SECRET; changing the secret invalidates all earlier credentials. No second user, session or outbox implementation exists. Security audit subscribes during people registration and registers its unsubscribe in ctx.cleanups. Password change retains only the caller's current browser session; reset invalidates every session and API token. Personal tokens cannot mint scopes broader than the caller's token. CLI groups may expose a handler.help string for credential-free --help; existing group help remains compatible.

Planning page boundaries are keyed by project, sprint or issue. The small planning-controls
module owns active request lifetime and controlled draft/latest decisions; it reuses the shared HTTP
revision, work paged-list and picker helpers. Project workflow impact comes from canonical status
counts in projects.js, while canonical sprint-history.js remains the sole scope/burndown ledger.
AttachmentQueue adapts the existing uploadAttachment streaming transport sequentially, with
one current AbortController, per-file results and explicit retries. Disposal aborts that owner
and prevents delayed callbacks from publishing into another resource. No additional
permission service, upload framework, history calculator or migration engine is introduced.


L0 completion centralizes CLI credential validation/atomic replacement in cli/config.js and preserves raw upload/response transport in CrewClient. Human formatting escapes terminal controls and retains opaque cursor navigation; JSON stays unchanged. Auth state owns one form request and suppresses abandoned responses. Overview consumes existing protected organization/project readers through scoped loads. The hash subscription rereads current location and the shell owns heading/skip focus, bootstrap error and explicit logout decisions. Server lifecycle.js owns listen readiness and one bounded cleanup/drain/close result; index.js adapts process signals and fatal asynchronous failures. No filesystem/history/runtime framework is added. See api-cli.md.

People administration reuses the existing planning request owner and insight scoped loading, including exact opaque route/resource identities. Organization, team and membership updates use the same canonical HTTP content revision helper as work; the old work import path remains a compatibility export. Member-access projections derive role capabilities and direct/dormant grants from canonical permissions, while existing project-guest routes remain the only grant mutations. Audit choices derive labels and counts from already-authorized sanitized audit events, avoiding a separate directory or additional token scopes. Local response abandonment does not undo an already accepted server mutation.
